name: 02-go-the-open-body-and-the-same-lookup-in-the-lessons-words
why: The first finding says Rate returns without closing the response body on any path, so each call leaves its connection held, and that the body should be closed with a deferred call once the request succeeds: that is the idea of the linked sentences on releasing what a function opens, said without the pattern's name, so the open body is found. The second says the loop asks for the same pair's rate on every pass although the answer does not change, and that it should be fetched once before the loop: the idea of the linked sentence on work that gives the same answer on every pass, so the lookup in the loop is found. 'Use http.DefaultClient' is a preference, and a poor one since the default client has no timeout: false positive. The ignored Decode error is not mentioned: missed.

key.consequence: Every call to Rate leaves the response body open, so its connection is never returned to the pool or closed, and a program that keeps converting runs out of connections and file descriptors.
key.explanation: Rate reads the response but never closes resp.Body, and Go keeps the connection busy until the body is closed. Put defer resp.Body.Close() right after the error check, so that it runs on every path out of the function.

judged.reason: The edit removes the deferred Close that the clean code puts right after the error check.

sentences.text: Whatever a function opens it must close on every path out of it, or the resource stays held until the program ends.
Close a response body with a deferred call right after the request succeeds, so that every return path releases it.

key.consequence: A response that is not valid JSON leaves body.Rates nil, and the caller is told that there is no rate for the pair, which hides that the service sent something broken.
key.explanation: Rate throws away the error that Decode returns, so a broken response is reported as a missing rate. Check the error and return it with the pair, as the other failures are.

judged.reason: The edit replaces the checked Decode with one whose error is assigned to the blank identifier, and the clean code returns it.

key.consequence: ConvertAll makes one request to the rates service for every amount, all for the same pair, so a long list is slow and may hit the service's rate limit, and the amounts can be converted at different rates if the rate moves during the loop.
key.explanation: ConvertAll calls Convert inside the loop, and Convert fetches the rate each time, though the rate is the same for every amount. Look it up once before the loop and scale each amount with it.

judged.reason: The edit moves the rate lookup from before the loop into Convert, which the loop calls for every amount, and the clean code looks it up once.

sentences.text: Work that gives the same answer on every pass of a loop belongs before the loop, done once.

review.text: Rate returns without closing resp.Body on any path. Each call leaves its connection held open, so a program that keeps converting runs out of connections. Close the body with a deferred call as soon as the request succeeds.
Each pass of this loop asks the service for the rate of the same pair, and that answer does not change from one pass to the next. Fetch it once before the loop and scale every amount with it.
Use http.DefaultClient instead of building a new client, it is simpler.
